Section cdc_child:000 is the title/'how to use' page of the 2025 CDC Child and Adolescent Immunization Schedule (Revised 07/02/2025). It contains no age-specific dose recommendations, so no rules were produced.

The vaccine product table (abbreviations and trade names, e.g. Beyfortus, Comirnaty, Spikevax, Novavax, Dengvaxia, Daptacel, Infanrix, ActHIB, Hiberix, PedvaxHIB, Havrix, Vaqta, Engerix-B, Recombivax HB, Gardasil 9, Flucelvax, FluMist, M-M-R II, Priorix, Menveo, MenQuadfi, Bexsero, Trumenba, Penbraya, Jynneos, Vaxneuvance, Prevnar 20, Pneumovax 23, Ipol, Abrysvo, Rotarix, RotaTeq, Adacel, Boostrix, Tenivac, Tdvax, Varivax) is product-choice information and is not represented. It could be used later to map products to concepts. Combination products such as Pediarix, Pentacel, Kinrix, Quadracel, Vaxelis and ProQuad count toward their component vaccine concepts.

The section mentions products with no exact concept in the vocabulary: maternal RSV vaccine (Abrysvo), split influenza formulations (IIV3, ccIIV3, LAIV3), and the combination MenACWY-TT/MenB-FHbp (Penbraya). No concepts were created because no rules were written.

General catch-up guidance is not represented: 'Administer recommended vaccines if immunization history is incomplete or unknown. Do not restart or add doses to vaccine series for extended intervals between doses. When a vaccine is not administered at the recommended age, administer at a subsequent visit.'

Several items are referenced but not present in this section: Table 1 (by age), Table 2 (catch-up intervals), Table 3 (medical conditions), the Notes, the contraindications/precautions appendix, and the ACIP shared clinical decision-making recommendations. Reporting instructions (VAERS, health departments) and contact information are administrative and not represented.
